title: No prepositions at the end, working backwards (unir), con que, cuál, quién / quiénes

cards.title: Prepositions never end a sentence
cards.body: 'Where are you from?' becomes 'from where are you?'. No 'the' before Estados Unidos.

examples.en: We're going to the United States.

cards.title: Working backwards: unidos → unir
cards.body: Strip the ending that was added (-ido means -er or -ir), then try both. Intuition for what sounds Spanish grows with listening.

cards.title: la chica con que trabajo
cards.body: 'The girl I work with' = 'the girl with that I work'. Que works for all of these; you'll also hear con quien, con la que, con la cual. La chica / el chico = the girl / guy (informal).

examples.en: It's the girl I used to work with.
examples.es: Es la chica con que trabajaba.

examples.en: the girl I was going to the party with
examples.es: la chica con que iba a la fiesta

cards.title: iba: like va with an i
cards.body: Iba blends -aba and -ía, or think of it as the present va with an i in front (spelled with b).

cards.title: cuál = which (one)
cards.body: Don't repeat the preposition at the end; that's negative transfer from English.

examples.en: I don't know which one he wants to see.
I don't know which one he wants to do it with.
examples.es: No sé con cuál quiere hacerlo.

cards.title: quién / quiénes = who
cards.body: Who goes with the he/she form; use quiénes when you expect more than one person. Location = estar, so '¿Quién está?' means 'who's there?'.

examples.en: I don't know who I have to do it with.
examples.es: No sé con quién tengo que hacerlo.

examples.en: … who I have to do it for.
examples.es: No sé para quién tengo que hacerlo.

examples.en: … who I have to do it because of.
examples.es: No sé por quién tengo que hacerlo.
